★ TREERING ARCHIVE EVIDENCE PROJECT: Needs Review → File is in inventory but has not been read or summarized yet. Default for newly added files.
Reviewed - Partial → File was opened or skimmed, but not fully analyzed. Use when content is promising but incomplete.
Reviewed - Verified → File has been opened and the key claim(s) were verified from content. Safe for evidence guide and resume drafting.
Duplicate / Derivative → File appears to be a copy, export, comment HTML, or alternate version of another file. Do not double-count; link to canonical file.
Skipped / Archive → File is low-value, media-only, system junk, or outside current scope. Only revisit if a related artifact points back to it.
Blocked / Not Found → Expected file could not be located or opened. Search later with alternate names.
Critical → Likely core portfolio/resume evidence. Review early and cite carefully.
High → Strong supporting evidence. Review in current lane.
Medium → Useful context, but not likely centerpiece. Review after high-value files.
Low → Probably archive, duplicate, or nice-to-have. Defer.
High → Claim is supported by file content. Safe to use with citation/receipt.
Medium → Claim has some support but needs another source or clearer context. Use cautiously.
Low → Lead only; do not use in final materials yet. Needs verification.
Performance analysis → Metrics, reporting, dashboard, or outcomes. Prioritize for resume bullets.
Campaign architecture → Sequence map, editorial calendar, persona matrix, QA plan. Prioritize for portfolio process story.
Training / enablement → Decks, guides, onboarding, workflow instructions. Use for leadership and enablement proof.
Meeting notes → Internal decisions, leadership context, product/process insight. Use for color and interview examples.
Call notes → Prospect discovery, objection handling, selling style. Use for sales style and case examples.
